name: Cricket Ball
summary: Glossy red leather shell with a subtle recessed equatorial join aligned to a raised central primary welt. Six rows of cream stitches are actual geometry, 72 stitches in each row (432 strands). Two shallow quarter-cover seams are thin geometry. Grain is a baked normal map.

Six rows of cream stitches are actual geometry, 72 stitches in each row (432 strands). Two shallow quarter-cover seams are thin geometry. Grain is a baked normal map. Static visual asset; no physics.
author: Yap Wei Jun project / agent-assisted procedural modeling
creation_method: Original deterministic Blender Python surface meshes and capped seam/thread tubes; Cycles-baked procedural tangent-space normal map. No external assets or markings.

display.origin: Actual floor contact point under the horizontally centred exported bounds

accuracy_notes: MCC Laws of Cricket, 2017 Code 4th Edition (2026), Law 4.1, adult men / Size 1: circumference 224–229 mm; midpoint 226.5 mm, diameter 72.097 mm. The outer shell is a continuous editable sphere; four cover regions are visually delineated by the primary and quarter seams, not separately cut leather solids. The six stitch rows use an illustrative 72 stitches per row, not a count specified by MCC. Five-sided thread and sampled seam tubes reduce geometry; no core or physical seam mechanics. Measured extents include raised seams/threads; nominal diameter describes the skin. Fine grain is normal detail only. Source: https://www.lords.org/getmedia/a4ef9f77-2a25-4f5b-a286-4601f08e6334/Laws-of-Cricket-2017-Code-4th-Edition-%282026%29_5.pdf
